ARC-Managed Layer Handle (Hierarchy-Aware)

Provides automatic memory management for Layer objects with parent-child relationship tracking to prevent double-free errors.

Key Challenge: When a Layer is added to a parent, destroying the parent automatically destroys the child. This handle tracks parent relationships to avoid destroying children that have already been destroyed by their parent.

Usage Example:

import nebble/ui/layer_managed

var parentLayer: LayerHandle
var childLayer: LayerHandle

proc windowLoad(win: ptr Window) {.cdecl.} =
  parentLayer = newLayerHandle(makeGRect(0, 0, 144, 168))
  childLayer = newLayerHandle(makeGRect(10, 10, 124, 40))
  
  # Add child to parent - parent now owns child
  parentLayer.addChild(childLayer)
  
  win.rootLayer.addChild(parentLayer.getLayer())

proc windowUnload(win: ptr Window) {.cdecl.} =
  # Only parentLayer is destroyed here
  # childLayer was already destroyed when parent was destroyed
  parentLayer = LayerHandle(nil)
  childLayer = LayerHandle(nil)  # Safe - checks parent before destroy

Imports

../ffi, ../ffi/managed, layer

Types

LayerHandle = object

Managed handle for Layer with parent-child tracking.

When added to a parent via addChild, the child tracks its parent to avoid double-free when the parent destroys children.

Procs

proc `=copy`(dest: var LayerHandle; src: LayerHandle) {.error.}
Copying disabled - use move semantics. 
proc `=destroy`(h: var LayerHandle) {....raises: [], tags: [], forbids: [].}

Destructor - destroys layer only if it has no parent.

If the layer has a parent, the parent will destroy it, so we skip destruction here to avoid double-free.

Limitation: If the layer is removed via C API (not through removeFromParent) or if the parent is destroyed first, this may cause issues. Always use the managed API for hierarchy operations.

proc addChild(parent: var LayerHandle; child: var LayerHandle) {.inline,
    ...raises: [], tags: [], forbids: [].}

Add child layer to parent. Parent takes ownership of child.

Important: After calling this, the child should not be destroyed directly. Destroying the parent will automatically destroy the child.

Example: parentLayer.addChild(childLayer) # childLayer will be destroyed when parentLayer is destroyed

proc removeChildLayers(parent: var LayerHandle) {.inline, ...raises: [], tags: [],
    forbids: [].}

Remove all child layers from this parent.

The children are NOT destroyed, just removed. They become orphans and must be managed separately.

proc removeFromParent(child: var LayerHandle) {.inline, ...raises: [], tags: [],
    forbids: [].}

Remove this layer from its parent.

After removal, the layer becomes an orphan and must be destroyed explicitly or added to another parent.
